force.title: The Hollow Middle
force.signature: The middle market collapses — shoppers split into premium and value, and anyone stuck selling undifferentiated mid-tier goods gets squeezed from both sides.

A \u00b7 The stores splitting apart: The mid-tier anchor of retail hollows out as shoppers go luxury or discount.
Trading down powers dollar, convenience, and value formats.
Affluent shoppers keep spending on jewelry, beauty, and status goods.
B \u00b7 Apparel & footwear bifurcate: Fast-fashion and luxury grow; mid-price apparel chains close.
Specialty and athletic footwear thrive; generic mid-tier shoe retail shrinks.
C \u00b7 Eating & staying out: Casual-dining middle empties as diners split between cheap fast food and premium experiences.
Budget and luxury/experiential lodging grow; the mid-scale motel struggles.
D \u00b7 Experience & status: Consumers trade goods for experiences and premium live events.
Cheap 'dupes' and private label eat the mainstream middle of consumer goods.
E \u00b7 The big picture: Capstone: the middle market is hollowing out; luxury and value win, undifferentiated mid-tier loses.
